items.title: Authentication & Sessions
items.description: Email/password auth with JWT cookies, bcrypt hashing, protected routes via global middleware, and automatic session refresh — no third-party auth vendor required.

items.title: Payments & Subscriptions
items.description: Stripe Checkout, Customer Portal, and webhook handling that keeps subscription state in sync with your database. Start charging from day one.

items.title: Teams & RBAC
items.description: Multi-user teams with Owner and Member roles, invitations, and member management UI ready to extend for your own permission model.

items.title: Postgres & Drizzle ORM
items.description: Type-safe schema, generated migrations, seeding, and a query layer that keeps database logic out of your routes and actions.

items.title: Activity Logging
items.description: An audit trail for every meaningful user event — sign-ins, invites, setting changes — surfaced in a timeline on the dashboard.

items.title: Marketing & Dashboard UI
items.description: Landing page, pricing page, auth screens, and a settings dashboard built with shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS v4, with light and dark themes.

items.question: What is included in this SaaS starter?
items.answer: Authentication with email/password, Stripe payments and subscriptions, multi-team support with role-based access control, a settings dashboard, activity logging, and complete marketing pages — everything you need to launch a subscription product.

items.question: Do I need a Stripe account to use it?
items.answer: Yes, for payment features. The included setup script walks you through creating Stripe products and prices locally, and the Stripe CLI forwards webhooks to your dev server so subscription events work end-to-end before you deploy.

items.question: Which database do I need?
items.answer: Any Postgres instance. The setup script can create a local database for you, and in production you can point POSTGRES_URL at Neon, Supabase, RDS, or any other managed Postgres.

items.question: Can I customize the theme and branding?
items.answer: Absolutely. All colors are CSS-variable design tokens, so switching the brand palette is a one-file change. Light and dark modes are built in, and the UI is composed of shadcn/ui components you fully own.

items.question: Is it free to use for commercial projects?
items.answer: Yes. The starter is MIT licensed — use it for as many commercial products as you like, with no attribution required.
